Greeting from Stockholm!

I fully agree, though Sweden has changed a lot recently—hidden corruption included. That said, our nature is unbeatable 😍. Honestly, this would be the best country to live in if we didn't have 6-7 months of constant darkness. The lack of sunlight really affects people's mood and mental health; Swedes are great at hiding how depressed they get during the winter!

comments.author: @Twosausagedogs
comments.text:
Also in Sweden: 
High unemployment: Among the highest in the EU.
Very high taxation: One of the highest tax burdens in the OECD.
High household debt: Among the highest household debt-to-income ratios in Europe.
Rising inequality: Sweden has experienced one of the fastest increases in income inequality among OECD countries.
High divorce rate & many single households: Sweden has one of the world's highest proportions of single-person households.
High antidepressant use: Among the highest rates in the world.
Very low hospital capacity: Only 1.9 hospital beds per 1,000 inhabitants.
Long healthcare waiting times: Persistent and comparatively long waiting times despite high healthcare spending.
